description: Somos Ghosts, un equipo de estudiantes de Ingeniería en Sistemas Computacionales compitiendo presencialmente en el Tecnológico de Zacatepec. Usamos Java, MySQL y herramientas de IA para crear prototipos funcionales con datos abiertos de la NASA
summary: What was developed was an interactive website that helps users navigate the Moon and Mars to learn about the history of some objects that have been forgotten (like the launch site and year, the mission's purpose, crew members, etc.) in the space missions from 1969 to 2025. The importance and the reason that led us to take on this challenge is that currently there is an endless amount of information about the space missions to the Moon and Mars, but not enough guidance—we don't know where to start looking or how much time we are willing to spend. This leads to a loss of interest in learning, especially for kids who want to learn while playing, without complications.
details:
The app starts working when the user chooses their exploration destination: the Moon or Mars. Once the destination is selected, they move through the virtual environment using their device’s arrows, guided by an integrated compass that shows the recommended direction and current geographical coordinates. During the journey, the user must dodge obstacles like asteroids while searching for historical mission objects (highlighted in blue). When interacting with an object, a story is shown in both text and audio, narrating the relevant history (location, launch year, crew, and mission purpose). As they accumulate discoveries, the user earns points that can be exchanged for fuel for their spaceship, allowing them to keep exploring new territories.

The project offers an interface designed to capture the audience's attention, mainly school-aged children, optimizing interaction time and facilitating continuous learning. By focusing the content concisely on the objects sent to explore the Moon and Mars, it avoids being overloaded with technical terms, stimulating students' imagination and curiosity without overwhelming them, and promoting an understanding of the history of these objects that have remained in space on the Moon and Mars for the last 60 years through visual and auditory resources.

The factors that were taken into account for the development of the project were:

1. Resource and capacity management: Evaluate the available time, team members' skills, and the tools we have to optimize our project.

2. Pedagogical design and attention span: Adapt the language to avoid complex technical terms and estimate the time needed to keep the user's attention (about 30 seconds).

3. Accessibility and inclusion: Include audio narrative options for users who are learning to read and easy-to-read text for those with hearing difficulties.

4. Comparative analysis with other similar websites regarding age, number of steps to complete the mission, information overload, technical terms, etc.

1. The tools that were used were:

1. Android Studio: Development for the design and overall structure of the page.

2. HTML5 and CSS3: Creating the code for the page and its interface.

Ibis Paint: Graphic software used for the digital illustration of the platform's graphic elements.

3. Canva: Creating the visual design of the project's slogan.

4. Google AI Studio: Artificial intelligence platform used to help with layout visualization and generating HTML code prototypes.

5. Space App Challenge: Collection of historical data on objects launched into space.

Use of Artificial Intelligence:

Claude and ChatGPT were used to rework the information, transforming it into a story adapted for younger generations.
